This entity allows the assessment batches available for a MAB to be defined. This is used to track which batches are available to add students to (as part of the student batch allocation screen), and also which batches are committed.
Defines the individual elements which make up an award confirmation rule (ACR).

Defines the elements of an award calculation method (ACM) which determine the credit minima and maxima and the levels from which the credits must come. All individual records can have a weighting but the sum of them all must be 100.

Defines the types of rules which are to be used to calculate the highest possible non-discretionary student award. The award calculation method produces an overall mark for a student which locates them (if the awards are classified) within one of the classes of the award. Their basic eligibility for an award will already have been determined if they have passed the appropriate award rules (AWR). The achievement of a class may also be subject to confirmation rules (ACR). It is possible to use an alternative award calculation method (ACM) as an award confirmation rule. The ACM specified on a confirmation rule must not be referenced elsewhere in that particular award (AWD) as this can potentially lead to incorrect calculations as SAV, SCR or SCD may be overwritten during processing. A student's class may also be upgraded or downgraded either automatically or at discretion by applying upgrade rules (AUR). Again, it is possible to use an alternative award calculation method (ACM) as an award upgrade/downgrade rule. The ACM specified on an upgrade rule must not be referenced elsewhere in that particular award (AWD) as this can potentially lead to incorrect calculations as SAV, SCR or SCD may be overwritten during processing. Up to three alternative award calculation methods are permitted, CAMS will select the highest award and classification achieved by any of the methods. It is possible to have multiple rules per classification for AUR or ACR. System parameter CAM04_036 determines whether a student must pass all or any of the rules associated with the classification to have their award confirmed, upgraded or downgraded.

Defines the award confirmation rules which are additional conditions which must be satisfied for an award classification to be confirmed. The rule is applied during the award calculation process. Award classifications which are not confirmed are downgraded one class.  Award confirmation rules are optional.

Defines the type of activity for topic elements. The entries in this table are used when creating event and topic element table records. It is a background record used in assigning rooms whilst taking into account the various ranks given to particular collections of activities. The MAR record is used to set up a link between similar room activities and provide a rank for them in order of preference when assigning the activity to a room format.
The Academic Standing Profile Element (ADE) entity is used to specify what Academic Standing Match Method (AMM) to use during an Academic Standing calculation, and when to use it.
The Academic Standing Profile is used to associate a set of Academic Standing calculation rules with a student, programme or module.

Assessment paper division requirement records identify that a particular division of an assessment paper, requires specific materials equipment such as paper and pencils, books, texts etc. The requirements can be added after the exam scheduling has taken place, specific records are not created for each student and assessment item which has requirements. Although you may not be using the concept of divisions and papers for the main assessment process, if you wish to manage resources you will require at least one assessment paper and division to attach to the module assessment pattern. It may be, therefore, that you only use it for specialist items of equipment which students are required to return at the end of the exam. The table requires the user to specify the number of items required per student sitting the division. The items themselves are validated by entries in the Assessment Requirements (ARQ) table.

Top level screen to view sections of assessment paper divisions. These records allow the user to subdivide an assessment paper division into sections defining a maximum and minimum number of questions to be answered. This record is intended for use within the CAMS Exam Questions facility. This allows the user to define individual questions for each student based on their MAP>MAB>>ATP>ADV, produce a spreadsheet to capture the marks for each question; monitor the marking of the questions; import those marks and then update the individual assessment records which use the questions.

Assessment Paper Division Maintenance Form (CAM_APS) - This table defines the divisions within an assessment paper. For example section A of Maths exam paper. This feature allows you to subdivide an assessment paper still further. The word division has been used as a generic term rather than using a word such as question which may be too restrictive. The division allows an assessment paper to be divided up into specific "parts". These divisions may be independently examined by a different examiner, for whom specific fees are paid. The user can also specify the equipment required for a division. If different combinations of "parts" can be sat then these need to be their own division. In the example, there is an assessment paper for English level II critical studies which potentially has three divisions which may be taken by different groups of students. AHL records can be created whenever a SMO record is updated. A batch process will then take all the AHL records and process the absence hours for the relevant students. The batch process is run from option XAHL.

The Adjustment Rule Condition (AJC) entity is used to create conditions that should be checked to see if an adjustment should take place. Only if a students profile of results passes the condition will the adjustment take place.

The Adjustment Rule (AJR) entity provides the header information for rules used to adjust module marks to be used in the calculation process. The adjustment can be either to calculate an updated module mark or to create an entirely new "magic" module both of which can be based upon a credit profile (e.g. update the mark on all level 1 modules with the average of the best 60 credits).

The Adjustment Rule Selection (AJS) entity is used to specify which records should be processed as part of an Adjustment Rule. It can either be set-up to generate a new module or to update the selected modules with a new mark.

The Adjustment Rule Type (AJT) entity is linked to the AJR and specifies the tasks that the rule should perform. It can either be set up to select and Update existing module results or Create new records which can then be used within the Awards Calculation process
The Adjustment Rule Update (AJU) entity is used to calculate an updated mark to be applied to all records selected by an associated Adjustment Selection (AJS) record.
The Alias table is used to link web users with pmu records.  Enabling online users to have simple and memorable user names.

Defines the different types of classification which may exist within a calculation method. When set up, these records will override any associated award classifications (AWC) when the associated calculation method (ACM) is chosen during award calculation. Note: Currently the records will only be used to determine the classification to use as part of a Award Calculation Element (ACE) and will not be applied at the Confirmation or Upgrade rules. They should also be set up in such a way that they only contain Classifications (CLA) that are defined on the associated AWC. Setting up AMC records with classifications that are not also in AWC may cause the calculation process to be unable to determine an overall classification.
The Academic Standing Method Element is a record that can be used to group calculation rules (PCM), and decide what to do based on the outcome from that calculation rule.

The Academic Standing Method Match table allows a set of calculation rules (specified on the element AME records) to be grouped together ready to be associated with an Academic Standing Profile (ADP).

Assessment Paper Maintenance Form (CAM_APS)- The assessment paper table allows you to define common exams which cross modules. Common exams happen where students are studying a similar subject within different modules provided by different departments. Normally there is a risk that students sitting the same paper could be scheduled to sit the exam at different times, thus increasing the chances of a "leak" or "compromise". The assessment paper is an independent record which can be attached to any module assessment pattern element. If you wish to manage the resourcing of the exams e.g. paper,equipment etc. you will need at least one assessment paper (APT) record per module which then references an assessment paper division (ATP>ADV)because assessment requirements (ARQ) are attached at the division level not higher.

This screen is used within student award prediction processing (as part of progression calculation) in order to define the maximum number of modules or credits that can be updated as part of the process.
The Assessment Paper Details Entity (APD.CAMS) allows you to define the attributes of a serial exam.

This table defines the divisions within an assessment paper. For example section A of Maths exam paper. It identifies when an Assessment Paper has been withdrawn from use but it does not have any interactive qualities.  It is probably helpful not to have too many.
Assessment Paper Type Maintenance Form (CAM_APT) - this is where different types of assessment papers are defined e.g. open book, experiment, language translation etc.

Award Predictor Results (APU) records are created each time the award prediction processes are run (either by e:Vision program SIW_XAWD or via student progression). These records contain the student and module result details that were used to form the basis of the award calculation, along with the details of the calculated award and classification.

Assessment Paper Requirements Maintenance Form (CAM_ARQ) - this is intended for the user to record the items of equipment which are needed for a specific assessment paper e.g. answer books, Bunsen burner, set text etc. There are reports which can then be produced which are either estimates or actual numbers of that specific item required for a particular assessment. The requirement is not attached at the assessment paper level but at the division level. Even if you are not scheduling common exams if you want to manage the resources of the exam timetable then you need at least one assessment paper and one division for each Module assessment body which is of the assessment type e.g. exam to be scheduled.

Assessment Paper Requirement Type (CAM_ART) - assessment paper requirement types allow the user to define such things as whether the item is re-usable, not re-usable. These types are reflected on the assessment paper requirements reports so that invigilators can be reminded to collect some items back.

Defines the type of assessment. It is referenced by the Module Assessment Body table, which defines in more detail how a module is assessed. The assessment type table defines the kinds of assessments that may be described in the assessment of modules. In defining an assessment type, you must be sure to apply a single type e.g. EXAM to assessments that you wish to process through the Examination Scheduling component of CAMS. Any controls defined in the remaining fields will be used by the module assessment pattern elements of this type unless the control fields are different in the element records themselves. The fields at the bottom of the screen control the sort order. The box on the left shows the criteria which can be used, the box in the middle is the order (ascending or descending), the box on the right is where the criteria which have been selected appear. The steps to make the selection are: 1 Click on the criteria on the left 2 Click on the order box and then the order required 3 Click on the Select button If the items in the selected box need to be changed: 1 Click on the item to be removed 2 Click on Clear When using the sort order, if the first criteria identifies an individual student then no other sort criteria can be used. If you use attempt number then an additional criteria can be included in the sort i.e. SPR number or name. If number is used and candidate keys are in operation then number would use candidate key rather than SPR number. You should remember that any controls such as print blind etc. which are applied to the Module assessment body records will continue to apply on the Module result form.

Event Change Request (ECR) The Event Change Request (ECR) record is created as a result of using the Timetable Review process (SIW_XECR) on e:Vision. A user such as a tutor, departmental staff or administrator can request a change to an Event before the final timetable is produced. These change requests can include week, day or time changes, or changes to the Personnel, Room and Facility Event Attributes (EVA) attached to the Event. Each time a request is made via the Timetable Review process, an ECR record is created. If any subsequent requests are made to the same Event, the original ECR record's status will be changed from Current to Superseded and the new ECR record's status will be set to Current. ECR records can be reviewed by the relevant administrator in the Modify Events (MEV) screen and the requested changes rejected or accepted. Any changes that are accepted can be made in the Modify Events (MEV) screen.

Provides the facility to record general information about exam centre visit logs. The exam centres visit logs are attached to the exam centre.

The EDT table incorporates all of the information required for an Electronic Distribution Table. This table is used for reporting purposes and is automatically populated and updated by a batch process using the main assignment submission tables.

Event Instance Change (EIC) records: These are an audit of every Event Instance (EVI) alteration where it has been identified that all associated Event Attributes (EVA) need to be re-evaluated to establish whether they could potentially be contributing towards a clashing timetable (EVA_RCSH).

Users can save their favourite Course, Programme, Route and Pathway selection. A record of what qualification a student hopes to attain. Field 39 (classification) covers institutions which allow enrolment to ordinary as well as honours degrees. Defines all timetabled events for each module occurrence for which events have been generated. This table is for display only, it would be unusual to enter an event record manually. The Event Clashes (EVL) table holds a list of events that clash with an event. It is used in conjunction with the Event Instance Change (EIC) table to ensure that the Reported Clash field on EVA can be kept up to date. This table is updated by the system automatically as part of the processing of EIC records and should not normally need to be changed manually.

The Event Programme Target entity is used to restrict the number of students with a particular profile (based on Programme, Level, and Mode of Attendance) who can be assigned to an Event (EVE). The information recorded on this record is associated with the equivalent information on the parent Event, which still controls the overall totals. The Class Size totals on the EVP records should add up, overall, to the # Students (Class Size) defined on the parent Event record.
The Event Quarantine Paper entity is used to define which papers are being taken during a quarantine exam event.

Provides the facility to record general information about exam centres. The exam centres are attached to the exam slot records once the exam slots have been generated via Assessment scheduling Profiles (ASP).  To add the exam centres quickly go to POG (program option group) Retrieve the code SI_RSQ. Click on the button at the end of the record. Select option 1 -Students in exam slots  from the set of options which appear.
The Extenuating Circumstance Linked Items record holds the details of the module or assessment item that has been affected by the extenuating circumstance.

The Feedback Access entity allows access to a particular type of feedback to be controlled using methods including restricting by MST, RGD, UGC or COM. It also allows an institution to define whether a user can override certain default values for a type (such as the category of feedback or whether the recipient should see the item).

The feedback bank entity holds items of feedback in a bank so they can be reused by a tutor/staff member. This might be a simple block of text or an attached document. Text entered as feedback is stored in the FBBN entity.
The Feedback Bank Note entity is used to hold the actual feedback content for the feedback bank. It is directly associated with the FBB table and is not used separately.
The Feedback Category entity can be used to specify the available categories of feedback that are available for use by staff members
The feedback bank favourites entity holds records of a user's favourites and the personal popularity of each feedback bank item.
The Feedback Group entity is used to group items of feedback together so that they can be associated with a student record (against SAS, SRA, SAQE, or SRQE in the first instance).
The Feedback Details entity holds information about a piece of feedback given to a student. This might be a simple block of text or an attached document.
The Feedback Details Note entity is used to hold the actual feedback given to a student. It is directly associated with the FBK table and is not used separately.

The Feedback Options entity is used to define any options that denote, for instance, what types of feedback are available for an assessment or question. This also includes things such as whether a user is permitted to access the feedback bank.

The Feedback Type entity is used to allow types of feedback to be defined. This might include whether the feedback should be a block of text or a file upload and whether the feedback should be shown to the recipient by default, etc.

Defines the different types of fee profile which determine the standard rate of fees to be charged for a module. This is defined on the Module (MOD).  Once defined the fee profile types are unlikely to be changed but the elements will do so since they are year specific.
Are used to specify precisely when events will run.

The Feedback Type Collection entity allows a group of Feedback Types to be created. These can then be made available to members of staff as part of the feedback options associated with an assessment element.

The GPP Elements (GPE) are used to determine the types of GPA calculation to be used. They can be accessed via the GPP other menu. For example, these could be overall, major or an other method. Additionally, each type has a corresponding Progression Calc Method (PCM).

The Holiday Collection is a group of dates (usually Bank Holidays). This group of dates is used in scheduling to not create teaching Events on these days.
Invigilator Job Requirements (IJR) holds individual jobs a member of staff might have, such as exam preparation, invigilation, exam clear-up, etc.

Location allows the scheduling process to be controlled in a way that is independent of actual sites.  The codes used may also be required by other administrative systems it is essential therefore that there is universal agreement on the structure and definition of each code.
