Learning Material Elements which make up sets. An Element is a learning material item one or more of which will form part of a set.

Learning Material Items.This field is validated by an entry in the LMI table and consists of any item which is used to support a student's study (12 characters). Each item may have many versions which can have a status of available, unavailable, planned or withdrawn. Collections of items (usually shrink wrapped for sending) are known as learning sets (LMS).

Learning Material Sets (LMS) are defined as collections of learning material items (LMI). LMS will normally be the level at which the institution re-uses learning materials across different module occurrences. Learning material sets are attached to the availability records (MAV) of modules. It is necessary to define these Learning Material Sets (LMS) using consistent coding strategies possibly relating to module code e g. beginning with EN for those sets attached to an English module. The 4 fields to be completed are code, short name, name and personnel.
Learning Material Task from LM versions
Each learning material item (LMI) may have many versions which may have a status of available, unavailable, planned or withdrawn. Different version numbers may differ slightly in volume, weight etc.
The Learning Outcome Category record can be used to record the categories available for use within Learning Outcomes (in particular on the Learning Outcome Link Element (LOE) record).

The Learning Outcome Contribution record is used to specify which items (e.g. assessments, modules, etc.) contribute towards meeting a specified learning outcome. It is attached to the Learning Outcome Link record so that items contribute to learning outcomes that are attached to parent records - for example you could specify that a particular assessment item contributes towards a module learning outcome or a pathway learning outcome.

The Learning Outcome Link Element record is used to hold additional details when a Learning Outcome Link (LOL) is repeated multiple times for the same linked record (e.g. multiple times for an assessment item), with different category or type information required each time.
The Learning Outcome Link is used to attach a particular learning outcome to a record, e.g. to attach a module outcome to a module.

The Learning Outcome Type allows you to define the types available for use on Learning Outcome (LOC) records. This might include things like Professional Requirements, Employability Skills, Learning Experiences, or just Learning Outcomes themselves.
The Learning Outcome holds the details about a learning outcome, professional requirement, etc.
The Learning Outcome Attainment Level allows you to define levels that can be achieved upon completion of a learning outcome.

Defines the travel times between locations which are taken into account by the student scheduler for students who need to attend the teaching events associated with a module which are taking place on different sites.

Learning Material Type code. This field is validated by an entry in the Learning Material Type (LTY) table. (12 characters).A disciplined and consistent approach is advised in creating an easily manageable and recognisable number of codes defining the type of learning material e.g. hardware, paper, coursework etc.

Defines the way in which levels can be formed into a collection. These collections may be used in the student programme planning rules and award calculation, confirmation and upgrade rules. Each level should be defined as a collection in itself. The levels making up the collection are defined in the Level Collection Element (LVE) table.
Defines the individual levels which make up a Level Collection (LVC).

This table allows the recording of UOLIA Administrator and Lead College Administrators for an assessment item (for use within certain Assignment Submission screens, restricting who can enter marks and allocate staff). This is in addition to Module Assessment Body (MAB). This table allows an institution to define a list of staff members along with their "role", but this is not used during the actual marker allocation processing - it is purely for use in restricting who can do what for an assignment. The Role field on the record is defined by us in terms of the available values (so they can be used in processing), but IFD can be used to override the translations for these values.

Defines the number and content of assessment items which make up an assessment pattern. These are defined by using a code, description of the assessment and the percentage weighting. The sum of all the assessment items must be 100. If assessment groups are being used then the sum of each set of assessment groups must equal 100%. The elements of an assessment pattern define each assessed item for a module. There can be many elements which are not necessarily all taken by the same students. The golden rule is however that each separate collection needs to be identified by an assessment group and must add up to 100% in total e.g. all the Agr A must equal 100 etc.

This table allows the user to define modes of attendance into collections.Mode of Attendance collection can then be defined on event route and occurrence route selection records to add additional refinement to who goes on which teaching activities. This allows greater freedom to set up occurrences aimed at part-time users only. Each mode of attendance should also be defined as collection of one.

Defines the types of assessments for a module and when these are due. It is currently used for enquiry purposes and generating reports. The default is for these details to be generated automatically when the student assessment records are generated. They can then be altered if required. These are automatically updated when Student Assessment Records are re-generated. System Parameter CAM_XSAS_13, allows the institution to prevent these records from being re-generated as part of any subsequent generation of Student Assessment Records.
Defines the individual modes of attendance which  make up the Mode of Attendance Collection record.

Used in the assessment process. Each module must reference an assessment pattern which describes both the weighting and methods by which a module is to be assessed e.g. coursework 50% and a 2 hour exam 50%. The Assessment Pattern is further defined by an Assessment Body which defines the number of assessment items which make up an assessment pattern. These are defined using a code, description of the assessment and the percentage weighting. The Assessment Body table can only be accessed via the Module Assessment Pattern table. Once the module assessment pattern has been defined it must be added to the Module (MOD) record. It must also be added the Module Availability (MAV) record. The code used on the module records generically defines how the module is assessed but the module availability table picks up any changes which happen from one academic period to another. If a Module Assessment Pattern changes,the old version must be retained. This is because there may still be students on the module for whom the old assessment pattern is still valid. If any additional results have to be added CAMS will not be able to find all the assessments if, for example, the pattern has changed from 3 to 2 items. The More details on "Other" then allows you to exercise control over output and data entry at the module result level. So it controls the order of students on the module result form and the levels of security etc. in the Process module results option within SAS,IAS,LAS or RAS. The fields at the bottom of the screen control the sort order. The box on the left shows the criteria which can be used, the box in the middle is the order (ascending or descending), the box on the right is where the criteria which have been selected appear. The steps to make the selection are: 1 Click on the criteria on the left 2 Click on the order box and then the order required 3 Click on the Select button If the items in the selected box need to be changed: 1 Click on the item to be removed 2 Click on Clear When using the sort order if the first criteria identifies an individual student then no other sort criteria can be used. If you use an attempt number then an additional criteria can be included in the sort i.e. SPR number or name. If the number is used and candidate keys are in operation then the number would use the candidate key rather than the SPR number. You should remember that any controls such as print blind etc. which are applied to the Module assessment body records will continue to apply on the Module result form.

Defines the types of rooms into which an activity may be scheduled by the CAMS Room Scheduler. The minimum size group permissible in the room is also defined. CAMS will attempt to schedule an event into the first room defined in the sequence, but if the group size for the event is below the minimum CAMS will attempt the next room in the sequence. If it is unsuccessful with all the rooms in the sequence an error message will be generated.

This record makes a module available for study within a particular year/period by defining the location, day, start time and target student number. The module must exist in the Module (MOD) table but until it is made available it cannot be selected, have teaching events generated for it or students scheduled onto it or be included in a module directory/handbook. The combination of the module code, Occ, Year and Period fields form one unique module availability record i.e. the same combination of data cannot be used twice.

This table holds a list of Personnel (PRS) who are performing specific activities attached to a Module Occurrence (MAV). Date ranges can be allocated to each staff member for an activity which can be used to keep track of when that person is performing an activity, and also allows for a simple clash check to be performed when making changes to these records. Each record links a member of staff to an Activity that is performed as part of the module occurrence. This may be, for example, a Class, Field Trip, etc.
Top level MAVT form

The MCQ Entity holds information that is required for marking a multiple choice questionnaire such as what assessment it relates to,what the negative marking factor is and what the correct answers are.

Module Changes Temporary Log (MCT) records relate to the filtering of module records for use within the FML Generation Process (GFML).  These records are generated when System Parameter (SYP) CAM_FML_001 = D (Deferred FML generation).
The Module Display Order (MDO) screen is used to group rules that determine the order in which modules are displayed within the basic version of the Module Registration selection screen (SIW_SME_C).

The Module Display Order Rule (MDR) screen is used to hold the rules that determine the order in which modules will be displayed within the basic version of the Module Registration selection screen (SIW_SME_C).

Provides a free text area to add more information about the content of the module. This information is extracted by the Module Directory process so it is important that the data defined is fit for external use.

Used in the assessment process, the module grade band table allows the grouping of similar grades into bands. This is for statistical reporting purposes only in order to accommodate marking schemes other than the standard A,B,CD. The maximum number of grade bands which can be accommodated is 9. The band code used is validate by an entry in the Scheme Grade Band (SGB) table.
This entity displays the Scheduling Group Elements (MGM) records are attached to a Scheduling Unit (MPG) record. These are used in the course of Module Scheduling.
This entity displays the Module Scheduling Unit (MGP) records used in the course of Module Scheduling.
This is used as a linking table between Scheduling Group Elements (MGM) and the Event (EVE) record to identify which Scheduling Group (MGP) relates to a specific Event record.

Defines the marks and/or grades associated with a particular marking scheme. It is extremely important that the grades and results represent exactly what you want to happen to a student during assessment. Check the CAMS Assessment Process Manual for more detail.
This entity defines which personnel have been contracted to mark a given exam paper and division. The records are used when assigning markers to sections of an exam paper.

Defines the marking scheme used in CAMS. An institution can have any number of marking schemes. The marking scheme is then defined in the Module Assessment Pattern.  The ranges of marks/grades which make up a marking scheme are defined in detail in the Mark Conversion Scheme (MKC) table which can only be accessed via the Mark Scheme table.  Separate marking schemes may also be required to deal with exemptions.

Full name: Marking scheme for assessment and re-assessment
Marking Scheme for re-assessment and award credit

Developer Help: Learning material on the Module Availability (MAV) record. This is where the user attaches the learning material sets to the modules available in a particular period.
Defines the individual parts of a module module rule and displays an English translation of the rule.
Defines the individual parts of a module module rule and displays an English translation of the rule.
A module module rule record identifies that there are rules which govern the taking of a module. The rules are then defined in the Rule Body (MMB).

This table defines the exchange value to convert the mark to for the purpose of calculating the classification for an award. Marks lying within the min and max boundaries are given the exchange mark for awards.
Defines the mode of attendance codes used in the collection of national statistics. Refer to the latest published guidance for a list of currently accepted values.
This entity is used to validate the Module Occurence value on a Module Availabilty (MAV) record. It is only used by the Tribal Edge application.
Defines general information about modules and their teaching activities. A more detailed description can also be entered in the Module Description table.
Defines the variety of modes of study available for a module, their value in staff contact hours and the optimum class size.

The Module Assessment Question Due Date (MQD) record is used to hold the current due date information for a particular assessment/re-assessment question.  Module Assessment Question Due Date (MQD) records are created/updated for both assessments and re-assessments via SAS options 1a (and SAS 1b where SYP CAM_XSAS_13 permits).
This table allows the reading list for a module to be recorded. You can assign different kinds of reading matter e.g. compulsory text, recommended etc.

The Scheduling Profile (MSP) record is created by the WASP exam scheduling process when exam scheduling is set to use MGP/MGM data. This scheduling mode can be enabled using system parameter CAM08_04.

Defines signals which are alphabetic coded messages that are sent by individual pieces of assessment that produce an outcome at the calculate module result stage of SAS,IAS,LAS, and RAS. The outcome is determined by the way you have specified the mark scheme table. This is the key bit that provides you with greater control. The number of implicit assumptions in the code have been removed. There are three levels of signals in their order of rank that can be set up in the signal status field: S Signals generated by the user which are the highest level Q Qualified signals only generated by CAMS when an assessment mark is less than the qualifying mark defined on the module assessment element N No signals The MSS table is used when the signal status in (MKS>MKC) is set to "S". The Mark Scheme Signal table is really a system table which should be modified with care. It is also best to keep the number for signals to a minimum to avoid confusion at the calculate stage.

Defines the way in which module types can be formed into a collection and used in student programme planning rules. The individual module types which make up the collection are further defined in the Module Type Element (MTE) table. CAMS automatically produces a module type collection for each module type added to the system. The collection has the same name and contains only one element, namely the module type.
Defines the individual elements which make up a Module Type Collection (MTC) record.
This table defines the specific details of an individual user's timetable, held as a variation on the Timetable Translation Group (TTG) record.
The MAV Occurrence Name entity is used to hold translations (the name) for what a particular MAV Occurrence value represents.

The MAV Programme Target entity is used to restrict the number of students with a particular profile (based on Programme, Level, and Mode of Attendance) who can take a particular occurrence of a module. It also records the current number of students on the module against those criteria. The information recorded on this record is associated with the equivalent information on the parent module occurrence record (MAV), which still controls the overall totals. The totals on the MVP records should add up, overall, to the values on the parent module occurrence record.
This table allows absence information to be recorded against Module Availably for a specific date.
This entity provides a free text area to add more information about the content of the module availability record.

Full name: MAV Descriptions - if changes are made

Developer Help: ANT//NTT Assessment Note Type. Referenced on the SMM table (SMR Minute); the SAN Table (Student Assessment Note) and the SRRN table (Student Reassessment Note). Used to describe different types of notes which may be associated with the student's assessment on/within a module - for example, where a student has a medical condition or is giving cause for concern.

Makes a topic option available for study within a particular year/period by defining the location, day, start time and target student number. The topic option must exist in the Topic Option table. All details for the Topic Option Availability record are generated automatically for compulsory topic options when the students are assigned to them. Each field must however be defined for each non-compulsory topic option record. The combination of the topic option code, Occ, Year and Period fields form one unique topic option availability record i.e. the same combination of data cannot be used twice.
This entity defines consequences of outcomes from academic standing

The topic option defines the topics which make up the topic. Where there is only one topic option defined, then the topic option is compulsory. Where there is more than one topic option defined for a topic the student can choose a maximum of one.

The topic option defines the topics which make up the topic. Where there is only one topic option defined, then the topic option is compulsory. Where there is more than one topic option defined for a topic the student can choose a maximum of one.

Use to limit a student's access to a specific module occurrence according to their Level/Programme/Route.  For example it is possible to direct students onto a specific route or conversely prevent students on a particular route taking a particular occurrence of module. This may be useful where students with different modes of attendance who are studying the same module need to be kept separate. Where there are module occurrence route selection records which give conflicting directions the record with a <Y> flag takes precedence.

Defines the way in which OUT codes can be formed into a collection and used in academic standing. The individual OUT codes which make up the collection are further defined in the OUT Collection Element (OTE) table. CAMS automatically produces a OUT collection for each OUT record added to the system. The collection has the same name and contains only one element, namely the OUT code.
Defines the individual elements which make up a OUT Collection (OTC) record.
This entity defines the outcomes available in academic standing
This entity defines the outcomes available in academic standing
This entity defines the outcomes available in academic standing
This entity defines the outcomes available in academic standing
The Override Calculation holds the details about the Override Calculation rule.
The Override Calculation Link contains the link between the Override Calculation (OVC) and its associated rules.
The Override Calculation Rule holds the information about the rule override.
The Programme Approval Group provides a method of controlling access to Programme Approval.

Defines different programme areas which can be used for external reporting and analysis.  The codes used may also be required by other administrative systems it is essential therefore that there is universal agreement on the structure and definition of each code.
Lists the awards which can be obtained for a defined Programme (PRG).

Defines the format of routes and the valid pathway types which can be used to build routes automatically. For example a pathway type such as major can be built into a valid route with one other pathway type - Minor.
Defines the individual elements which make up a Pathway Confirmation Rule (PCR).

Defines the method of calculation for a confirmation type rule to be applied to a pathway. Confirmation rules are optional rules which apply additional conditions which must be satisfied for an award classification to be confirmed e.g. must have obtained a minimum of 70 marks for a dissertation type module. The confirmation rule is applied during the award calculation process. Award classifications which are not confirmed are downgraded by one class. The elements of the rule are defined in the Award Pathway Confirmation Rule Element (PCB).

The Prescribed Diet Rule Inclusion (PDI) table is used to specify which diets, diet elements and periods should be included within a diet rule. When processed during submission, these records will be grouped by Type and selections matched against each one. Matching records will then be summed (e.g. credits counted) and compared against the Rule Value (PDV) record to see if that particular rule is passed.
A list of modules assigned to a standard programme (PDS). Modules must be associated with a particular PDM.  Available via the PDS other menu.

The Prescribed Diet Rule table is used to associate rule sets with a Diet (PDT). These rule sets allow an additional level of diet rule to be created which allows for rules between different diets and/or diet elements, and allows for credit limits to be defined per period.
Defines a prescribed diet selection for a related diet (DMD). Modules can be assigned to the diet selection via the associated prescribed diet selection module list (PDL) records.
This is used as a header in the creation of a diet of modules.

The Prescribed Diet Rule Value (PDV) table is used to specify the minimum and maximum values to check for a particular set of inclusions as part of a Diet Rule, along with specifying when and how the rule element should be applied.
The Prescribed Diet Category (PDY) entity is used to define a category for a Diet Element (PDM1) record, for example, Core Modules, and specify the order of importance using the Rank field.

This screen allows you to look at the snapshot records which have been extracted by the Generate Pathway Statistics (GPS) function.There are also Current and All options on the menu bar from which you can generate and print or just generate standard letters which have been defined in the Standard Letter (SRL) facility.The Current option only produces a letter for the student currently selected whether it is part of a larger retrieved list of records or not.The All option will generate a letter for each of the students retrieved.You should refer to the MENSYS Process and Reference manuals for more guidance on this. The record is longer than the screen. You can use the cursor keys to scroll up and down the total record.The top three lines of the screen always remain in view as a reminder of the student snapshot being accessed.  The record is divided up as follows:  1) above the line is Student Pathway (SPY) and Student Programme Route (SPR) information; 2) below the up to and including Home postcode is Student (STU) information.

Defines modules which are compulsory for a pathway and are also fixed in time i.e. can only be studied in one particular period. This record is then used to generate module selections automatically for those students taking the specified pathway. It used because:  *    it speeds up creation of large volumes of selection record;  *    reduces number of errors associated with mass data entry;  *    reduces risk of students accidentally omitting compulsory modules;  *    data need only be entered in Foundation record once unless there is a change to the pathway.

Defines the way in which PIT codes can be formed into a collection and used in pathway progression. The individual PIT codes which make up the collection are further defined in the PIT Collection Element (PIT) table. CAMS automatically produces a PIT collection for each PIT record added to the system. The collection has the same name and contains only one element, namely the PIT code.
Defines the individual elements which make up a PIT Collection (PIC) record.

Maintains Progress Information Template (PIT) data. Progression Information Type (PIT) table defines the progression codes to be applied to students as a result of the progression process. PIT codes are attached to the Matched Progression Method Elements (MPM>MPE) together with one or more Progression Calculation Method (PCM). The purpose of the PIT code is to denote the outcome of passing or failing the set of Progression Calculation Method (PCM) rules. The calculated PIT code is assigned to the Student Progression Information (SPI) record once the initial progression process has run. The agreed PIT code is determined at the Confirmation stage (the original can be retained or altered after the Board's decision). The Edit fields determine whether or not data is editable within the CSP Confirm Progression screen. If the fields are ticked (i.e. set to Y), users may amend field values within the CSP Confirm Progression screen. If the fields are unticked (i.e. set to N), it means that users cannot alter the data manually or via the Global Update facility. The fields are only available on the top level PIT table.
Pick List Interception records are used to omit, block, or report upon the creation of Pick List Header (PKH) records when certain conditions are met.
Defines the individual elements which make up a Pathway Module Rule (PMR) by identifying the modules required.
Defines the relationship of a module to a pathway. This table is used when checking the "legality" of a student's selections in relation to their chosen programme of study.

A pathway module rule record identifies that there rules which govern which modules can be taken on that pathway. The elements which make up the collection of information are defined in the Pathway Module Rule Elements (PME).
Questions completed by user on new user registration.  The user will be asked these questions in the event that they forget their login password.

Full name: PMU Questions - for use when user has forgotten th

Developer Help: Defines the individual elements which make up a Programme Rule (PRR).

Defines the types of time classifications used within a scheme e.g. terms, semesters. The number of periods i.e. slots which make up a year and the start and end dates of the slots is further defined in the Period Slot (PSL) table. The codes used may also be required by other administrative systems within the institution, it is essential therefore that there is a universal agreement on the structure and definition of each code.

Defines the programmes of study available within a scheme e.g. a Bachelor of Arts. A programme has an award attached to it e.g. Honours which is defined in the Programme Award (PAW) table. A programme consists of a valid route or route(s) which are defined in the Programme Route (PRU) table.

Defines a particular rule which governs the study of a programme. Programme rules usually specify the taking or passing of specific modules which are defined in the Programme Rule Element (PRB) table.

Defines basic details about the staff resources used to teach and counsel students on courses/modules.  The codes used may also be required by other administrative systems it is essential therefore that there is universal agreement on the structure and definition of each code.
Defines all the routes (ROU) that are valid for a particular programme.
Contains a breakdown of the subjects studied by the student enrolled on this course block.  This table is required to accommodate HESA.

This table contains the statistical records generated by the Generate Pathway Statistics (PWS) process using the Pathway Statistics Header selection criteria defined above.The report can also be printed via the PWS screen.The printed version of the report is in landscape format. The pathway figures are calculated based on the date in the Date field of the selection criteria.In the example the date used is the 20th August 1993.In Year 1 therefore there is one student on the AMSM pathway, this student will therefore have a start date his/her SPR record which fell in the academic year 1992/93.The 8 students in Year 5 on the AMSM pathway will have a start date in their SPR record which fell within the academic year 1988/89. If the census date had been 20th August 1988,the number of students in the Year 1 field for the AMSM pathway would be 8.

This table describes the selection criteria on which records will be extracted.Everything following the code and description is a selection criteria. If you do not wish to use a certain selection criteria leave the field blank.
Defines the number of weeks within a period.
Defines the individual elements which make up a Pathway Type Rule (PTR). These define the minimum and maximum credits to be obtained either at a certain level or of a certain type e.g. dissertation.
Lists the areas of teaching capability of a member of staff and their FTE value.
This entity records information about personnel tasks.

Defines rules which can be applied to a pathway type. These govern the number and type of modules to be taken at a specific type of level or levels. The individual elements are defined in the Rule Element (PTB) table.
Defines the individual elements of a pathway upgrade rule (PUR).

Define optional rules which invoke an additional check which may lead CAMS to recommend a student for a higher class of award. The upgrade recommendation can be automatic or discretionary. They typically identify borderline students who could be upgraded by one class within the rules of the scheme and require CAMS to look at the type of module results obtained e.g. more weight placed on higher level modules at the expense of lower level modules.

Defines the way in which pathway types can be formed into a collection and used in Student Programme Planning rules. The individual pathway types which make up the collection are defined in the Pathway Type Element (PWE) table.
Defines the individual pathway types which make up a Pathway type Collection (PWC). A single pathway type also needs to be defined as a collection for programme planning purposes.
This table is used to classify pathways into academic groups. These groups are used in the planning process.

Defines the different types of pathways available within a scheme. A pathway defines a named way for a student to progress through a scheme e.g. English major. All pathways must have a valid Pathway Type (PWT).  The rules which apply to all pathway types e.g. Major are defined by the Pathway Type Rule table.

Defines pathways which are named ways for a student to progress through a scheme e.g. English major. Combinations of pathways known as routes e.g. FRAHS could be a route French and History which is made up of two separate pathways French Joint and History Joint.

This table groups rooms with specific attributes together and is used by the CAMS Room Scheduler. These attributes may be based on something other than subject or type of activity for which they are used e.g. C1 - reserved for short courses, C2 - usual student accommodation. When each room (ROM) is defined the category can be included as part of the record. The category may then be built into a Room Scheduling Profile (RSP) record.

Defines the classes of rules which are to be implemented, it is almost like the "strength" of the rule. All rules must have a valid rule class. This is a system table which should only be changed with extreme caution. The following are valid. COMP must be observed OPEN rules that have no body because they reference data not in CAMS, e.g. must be able to play the violin RECO recommended but not compulsory
This table is used to convert CAMS results into HESA format.

Defines time elements which can be applied to rules. All rules must have a valid rule existence. This table is a system defined table and should only be changed with extreme caution. CO means required at the time NON negative of REQ POST will be required after PRE required before REQ has no time dimension, i.e. can be required at any time
Defines the room format for the room. The entries in this table are used to include room setup times as part of room clash checking processes when booking a room to an event(s).
Defines the types of text used by module reading lists. It is intended that this data will be reported on in some format to be agreed.

The Room Reservation for Departments (RMR) screen is used to define periods of time when Rooms (ROM) in defined Room Collections (RMC) are reserved for a Department (DPT). The RMR record can be set up in a number of different ways: Date Range - the RMR will be valid between a start and end date. Academic Week Range - the RMR will be valid between a start and end academic week. A start and end day is also required. A start and end time can optionally be added. Permanently Reserved - the RMR record is permanently reserved, i.e. is not specific to a date range or academic week range. The RMR will be checked when a ROM is added on any of the following processes/screens: Topic / Course Room Required (TRR) Course Block Timetable (CBT) Frequency Element (FQE) Event Attribute (EVA) Event Attributes (EVA1) Event Attributes (Active Week View) (EVA2) Event Attributes from Event (CAM_EVA3) Event Attributes from Attribute (CAM_EVA4) Event Summary (EVS) Generate Events (GEV) Event Modification Wizard (EVW) WGEM - Request Room Schedule Events to Room (SER) Assign Event to Room (AER) The User System Parameter (USP) CAM09_03 can be used to control whether the user is given the option to override the Room Reservation check when adding a Room (ROM) manually to an Event (EVE) or when adding a Room (ROM) on the Course Block Timetable (CBT), Topic Element (TEL), Topic / Course Room Required (TRR) or Frequency Element (FQE) screens. The system will check whether the ROM is available to the associated Department (DPT). If the USP is set to N, the user will be presented with a popup message asking them to select another room. If the USP is set to Y, the user will be presented with a popup message asking them to select another room or force the room to be added. The RMR checks can be turned on or off using System Parameter (SYP) CAM09_04. For more information please see the online manual.
Defines the individual pathways which comprise a route. A route can be made of just one pathway.

Defines the rooms which are located in a specific building. The data can be used by the CAMS Room Scheduling facility to schedule events into the room.  The room table defines the capacity and type of use to which the room can be put based on activities defined in Room Type (RTY) and also by a Room Category (RCA) which signifies certain attributes for the room.  The codes used may also be required by other administrative systems it is essential therefore that there is universal agreement on the structure and definition of each code.

Routes define valid combinations of pathways which a student can follow under a particular programme. For example a student who opts for a programme of study e.g. BA Hons could select a route such as American Studies Joint AND Political Studies Joint. The different elements of a route are called pathways. A route may only comprise one pathway.  The individual pathways which make up the route are defined in the Route Element (ROE) table. In the case of the example there would be two route element records.
Route (ROU) Reporting Data (RRD) table holds extra data regarding particular routes for the purposes of HEIMS statutory reporting.

The element record is the basic means to control how CAMS schedules the rooms. It determines the order in which CAMS attempts to select appropriate rooms for events. The room scheduling profile record can be manipulated in many ways and you must select the approach which best suits your institution. But before you schedule the rooms you must decide your priorities and strategy, this will then determine how you use the scheduler.

Defines a specific set of criteria which are to be used to schedule events to rooms.  The individual elements which make up the profile are defined in the Element record which is accessed via this table.
Defines which subjects are specific to a room e.g. a particular laboratory may only be suitable for chemistry.

The data in this table is used to define the elements which make up a route type rule.  The element is defined in database format which is then translated into an English statement for checking.  The element record uses module type collections which can be modified without having to modify the rule itself.

Contains the phrases which precede the rules which are defined and translated within CAMS e.g. "To obtain an award you must". The phrases are specific to a combination of:  Rule Class e.g. compulsory Rule Existence e.g. pre-requisite Rule Type e.g. module module rule

The data in this table is used to define route type rules which check during the award calculation process that the student has a certain number of credits from the relevant route elements (pathways) which make up the route.  An example of rule for a student studying a major minor type route would be "must have 7 credits from the first pathway and 3 credits from the minor pathway".  You may also specify the type of credits if necessary e.g. the first pathway (major) must have 2 credits of dissertation type.  The rule is referred to indirectly from the Classification Selection Conditions (ACM>CSR>CSS) which contains a flag field asking if Route Type rules are used.  The route type rule record is purely a header record which defines the level from which the credits must come.  The definition of the rule itself is contained in the Route Type Rule Element (RUT>RTR>RTB).
Defines the different types of rooms which may be used for teaching purposes.

The data in this table is used to define the different types of routes on which students can study e.g. major/minor and Joint.  The route type is then attached to the relevant routes.  The route type can have rules attached to it which are used in the award calculation process to control the types of credits being used by the process.  You need only set this table up if the award calculation rules are such that the type of credits used in the calculation process are subject to certain constraints. Students studying on a "JointJoint" type route must have 5 credits from the first pathway element of the route and 5 from the second.

Contains data used for analysis purposes.  It may be used to define externally determined types of analysis or to group types of information together.  There should be a universal agreement on the structure and definition of each code.

Contains data used for analysis purposes.  It may be used to define externally determined types of analysis or to group types of information together.  There should be a universal agreement on the structure and definition of each code.

Contains data used for analysis purposes.  It may be used to define externally determined types of analysis or to group types of information together.  There should be a universal agreement on the structure and definition of each code.

Contains data used for analysis purposes.  It may be used to define externally determined types of analysis or to group types of information together.  There should be a universal agreement on the structure and definition of each code.

Contains data used for analysis purposes.  It may be used to define externally determined types of analysis or to group types of information together.  There should be a universal agreement on the structure and definition of each code.

Records any award credits which a student may have gained than through the normal assessment process. It removes the necessity of having to register students on specific modules and generate dummy records for them. This may include students transferring from one institution to another part way through an existing course and who need to be credited for the work already done in order to meet the minimum number of credits award rule.
This entity holds the student standing result

This table contains details of the assessment records due for a particular module result record. This due date can be modified if appropriate along with actual date of receipt of the assessment in the case of coursework etc. These date fields can be used to perform mark modifications where an institution imposes penalties for late submitted work.  The personnel can record who received the work. Additional notes can be recorded about the receipt of work via the Assessment notes table which is accessed via the "Other" menu option. The assessment pattern and sequence numbers etc. are generated at the point of the record generation performed via the student Assessment (SAS) or Individual Assessment (IAS) options.

Provides top level access to notes recorded against an item of assessment.These notes can be printed in report form for submission to an examiner. The screen can be accessed via the student's individual module result record accessed via SPR. Complete the top section of the screen with the criteria for selecting the correct assessment records.

Reference Tables used in Student Annual Progress.  Decision Table 1  pass 2  fail 3  decision deferred 4  partial pass 5  not considered  Progress Table 1  course completed 2  continuing 3  conditional continuing 4  not continuing/no resit  Action Table 1  resit 2  1st attempt 3  repeat year 4  outstanding requirements

The Student Assessment Question Log (SAQL) record is used to record the receipting of assessment questions.  The structure is very similar to the Student Assessment Log (SAL) records which are used for the receipting at the assessment level.  SAQL records are generated via SAS 1b where assessment questions and logging is in use.

This option provides top level access to the module assessments for each module being taken by the student.  It displays the year/period and both the actual and agreed marks.  The most common reason for accessing this table will be to make global changes to a due date defined in error or which has been changed for all students.  You should limit the access to this table and only make edits to the data with great care.  You should not enter data in the screen.
The Student Award Variable (SAV) entity holds the results of the variable calculations produced by the Award Calculation process.

Records details of the awards which a student obtains during their programme of studies.  It is generated as a consequence of the PSA process. The award record displays the stage the student is at in the award calculation process and the award name to appear on the certificate.

Defines the detail of how a student's award result was calculated. This includes any upgrade/confirmation calculations which may have been used whether or not the student passed the rules controlling such calculations.  The data in this table is generated automatically by the Process Student Award (PSA) process.
This table defines to which modules each correspondence item defined in the Correspondence Element table refers.
Defines the schemes that are being operated and the student FTE credit value. The levels within the scheme can also be viewed.

Lists the modules to which the correspondence item refers.  You can delete or alter the list of modules to which the correspondence item refers should the student module results change before details have been despatched.  It also updates the list in the more detailed RSC.
Defines the students for whom correspondence has been printed which contains the correspondence item defined at the top of the screen.

Records details about the method used to calculate a student's award and the award classification. These are recorded in more detail in the Calculation Detail table. The award recorded may not necessarily be the same as the final award recorded in the SAW table, since the board responsible for considering award classifications may have determined a different classification.

Student Diet Module (SDM) records relate to the filtering of module records for use within Module Registration (SIW_MRG).  These records are generated by the Generate Student Diet Module (GSDM) process.
The Student Diet Override (SDO) table can be used to override minimum and maximum values on a Prescribed Diet Element record for individual students
The Student Diet Module Reason (SDR) entity is used to hold the reason for a Student Diet Module (SDM) being unavailable, which may include that a co-requisite hasn't been met, a module is full, etc.
Scheduling Group Constraints  This table holds information about a Scheduling Group's constraints so that these requirements can be taken into account when scheduling.
Defines individual subject groups which make up the programme areas.  These provide an additional level of details for analysis and external reporting.
Defines type status in relation to an available module. A - available - is the only acceptable entry. This is a system table and should not be changed.

Defines sites within which buildings and rooms can be located. The data is used during the Assign Rooms process (EVE) to assign rooms to events. The Rooms table defines the capacity and type of use to which a room can be put based on the types activities defined in the Room Type (RTY) table.  The Building and also Room tables can only be accessed via this table. The Room Events table which lists the events which have been assigned to a room can only be accessed via the Room table.

The data in this table is used to define the scheme and the level of a module. The records are ranked together with a flag indicating whether students are required to qualify, as defined by the pathway type rule, before taking modules of a higher level.
Student Learning Material Student record of Learning Material assigned to student during generation.
The Student Learning Outcome record holds details about skills attained from completing a learning outcome defined by a curriculum element.

The Student Module Application (SMA) table holds information on module applications that are made for study or for competency / exemption. The Student Module Application (SMA) records are populated using data from the Pathway Foundation Modules (PFM). Credits achieved can be transferred to Student Module Credits (SMC) records, whilst applications to study on a module can be transferred to Student Module Selection (SMS) records, by the Applicant Transfer ATR) process.

Records any credit (passed or taken) for a module which a student may have gained other than through the normal assessment process. It removes the necessity for dummy registration on the module and subsequent result processing. This may include students transferring from another institution part way through an existing course and who need to be credited for a specific module which is a part of a pre-requisite rule for a module they wish to take.
The SMCQ table holds a students answers for a multiple choice questionnaire. These answers are compared against the correct answers on MCQ to calculate a result.

Details the minute which relates to the module result. The minutes may have been added during the Process Module Result stage of the assessment process, or added directly into this record. If added at this point before the Process Module Result stage the minutes will appear on the Module Result form otherwise they will appear on any Exam Board Minutes printed after the module results have been processed. A student can have one minutes record per module.

Records the actual modules being taken by a student. The details in this table are generated automatically as a consequence of the scheduling process. The data for this table would normally be entered manually. Any editing of the detail must be treated with extreme caution.
The Student Module Taking Things (SMOT) entity is used to hold additional values that are related to the SMO but which are not always required.

Records the module result for each module being taken by a student. It displays the year/period and both the actual and agreed marks. The individual assessment results which make up a module result can also be accessed from this table. The details in the Module Result table are generated automatically as a consequence of the assessment process.
Top level SMRT form

Records students' choice of modules, ranked in order of preference. Usually the compulsory modules would be entered first, with the high rank numbers, followed by the optional modules. The modules in this table may not necessarily be the modules which a student ultimately studies.
A Record to contain an audit of the scheduling of the SMS record with which is has a 1 to 1 relationship with, thus will have the same Primary Keys as the SMS record.

The Student Module Waiting (SMW) table is a record of Students against Module Availabilities (MAVs). Each record is one SPR code waiting for one Module Availability in date/time order. One student can only be waiting for a module once. The purpose of this table is to ensure Students that cannot attend a full Module are placed fairly in a queue, should a space become available
This entity holds a module exclusion for a student (either for an entire STU or a specific SPR)

Records any award credits which a student may have gained other than through the normal assessment process. It removes the necessity of having to register students on specific modules and generate dummy records for them. This may include students transferring from another institution part way through an existing course who need to be credited for the work already done in order to meet the minimum number of credits award rule.

Student Progress Information GPA (SPIA) is created after a Progression Calculation method (PCM) is run (via XGPA). There can be one or more SPIA records and each is related to a Student Progress Information (SPI) record; the SPIA form can be access from the SPI other menu. The SPIA records hold data about each GPA calculation, including the GPA, and are generated using the GPA Profile Elements (GPE) parameters.

Student Progress Info Compensated Modules (SPIM) lists information about a student's module results after the Automatic Compensation process has been run. These records are overwritten each time the process is run.
This entity holds the results of module standing and programme standing processes
This screen display the credits that are used in the programme planning process

Student Pathway Progression Information (SPPI) record is a key record within the CSP Progression process for pathway type progression. SPPI is required for the Progression process to run, and records the outcome of the process. There is one SPPI record per pathway, and one SPI (Student Progression Information) record per course.

The Student Pathway Progression Calculation (SPPIC) record holds details about the calculation(s) performed during the pathway progression process. The SPPIC table includes information on the Progression Rule Element (PRE), the calculated value and whether the rule is true (T) or false (F). The confirmed values will be automatically populated when the pathway progression result is confirmed through CSP, and would be removed if the student's pathway progression result is later undone.

Defines information about students including their location, academic counsellor and programme route. This is the key entity for the CAMS (modular) system. Most details in this table are generated automatically as a consequence of a transfer process from the institution's normal student information database. The SPR table is the only means of access to all the tables listed in the Referenced By section. There are a great number of them and for this reason the purpose of path and references e.t.c. for each will be described as the tables occur alphabetically.

Details each piece of re-assessment which has been generated for a student, including the due date of the re-assessment and the actual and agreed marks. This record is generated automatically from the Student Re-assessment (RAS) process from within the Assessment component. Details of a student's re-assessment would not normally be entered here.
This table records the comments made by students and tutors as part of the module registration approval process (View/Add Comments).
This entity is used to log changes to a student's programme route.
The Student Diet Rule Override (SRO) table can be used to override minimum and maximum values on a Prescribed Diet Rule Value record for individual students

The Student Re-assessment Question Log (SRQL) entity is used to record the receipting of re-assessment questions. The structure is very similar to the Student Re-Assessment Log (SRR) records which are used for the receipting at the assessment level. SRQL records are generated via process module results (SAS option 8, RAS option 6, TMR etc.).

Student Rule Waivers (SRW) are used to identify different types of student rules to be waived during the Module Registration Process. MMR, PDV and Diet Rules are all examples of rules that may be waived.
The Student Selection Module Rule Result (SSM) record is used to record the outcomes from the Module Module Rule Validation (XMMR) process.

This table records the number of modules to be scheduled for a student during a particular year and period. Users need only specify the "Number of Modules", if the student is to be scheduled onto a different number of modules from the default number on the Student Scheduling screens (taken from SYP CAM02_04). There is a notes field to define reasons for differences etc. SSN is also required for the module registration facility on e:Vision. If necessary, create the SSN records via the POG SI_SCH (Student Scheduling utilities). The Registration Status is updated by the module registration process, to indicate if the selections have been entered (ENT) or confirmed (CON).
This is the header record for collections of Student Status (STS) records.
This is the element record for the collection of Student Status (STS) records.

This entity records information about student tasks, which are used during the exam tracking process. These records can be created during the 'Create Student Exam Question Records' and 'Student Assessment Marks' processes.

Records the actual topic options to which a student has been assigned.  The details in this table are generated automatically as a consequence of the assign student process.  The data for this table would not normally be entered manually.  Any editing of the details must be treated with extreme caution.
Defines the status of a student within CAMS. This is a system table which should only be altered with extreme caution.

Defines general personal details about a student for reference and correspondence purposes. This corresponds to the STU data provided by the Students Records System. The data cannot be amended here and automatically update SRS. Any amendments should be made to the master student records system.

Defines broad subject areas which are used to classify a member of staff's field expertise in their Teaching Capability record. The table is also used to classify subject areas according to externally defined criteria. From these, subject management reports for external use can then be generated. Users are advised to define broad subject areas to which staff can be allocated within their teaching capability record as well as specialist areas. The subject range should be such that the divisions represent levels at which staff resources can be considered suitable for teaching purposes. Example using History Social & General Ancient European Intellectual History History History History In the above example staff teaching any of the specialised subjects could teach General History. Similarly Staff teaching Social & Intellectual History could theoretically make some input to the period based subjects. This ensures optimum use of all staff resources.
This screen holds a workload adjustment for a student ( either for an entire STU or a specific SPR record)
The TAP entity records every 'TAP' or swipe of an individuals registration card, recording key data such as date, time, Card Id, and Card Reader Id.
TCO allows for the configuration of Timetable Constraints for Module Scheduler.
Defines how a particular topic is to be taught. This may be a combination of methods, in which case there will be two topic element records for the one topic record.

Defines patterns for topic elements which are used on a frequent basis. The topic element defines how a particular topic is taught. The pattern contains all the information required so that when creating a topic element record you can call up a pattern when in the Copy Pattern field, thus saving time and reducing the possibility for error during input.

This table is used to link the Translation (TTR) records to the Translation Group (TTG) records. It is also used in conjunction with Master Record Timetable Value (MTV) records to define the records viewed in the Translation Group (TTG) on a user basis.
This table defines the retrieve profile information that is requested upon running each of the options within Timetable Translation Group (TTG).
Defines the names of the working days and their individual start and end times.

Defines different types of time which are fundamental to the concept of concurrent and simultaneous teaching events which are used in the generate events process. This is a system table which should not be changed by the user.  The codes used in this table may also be required by other administrative systems within the institution. It is essential therefore that there is a universal agreement on the structure and definition of each code.
,The TMT entity links Individuals (via MST code) to Id card(s) they are provided with.
Defines the separate subjects to be taught within the module; one subject constitutes one topic and therefore one entry in the table.

This table links each Translation Group Profile (TGP) record to a Translation (TTR) record and a specific field on the Entity, defined in the TTR. Note: The TTR still needs to be defined in the TGE record in order for it to be shown in the timetable.
For use in Module Scheduler, the TPS entity holds a series of Day Slot (DYS) records linked to a Timetable Constraint (TCO) record.
,The TRM Entity links ID Card Readers to the rooms in which they are situated.
Timetable Constraint Room Split (TRS) records can be used to determine the preferred and maximum number of rooms that can be used for a room split.

This table defines the colours that are available for different aspects of the timetable, and where they should be applied. The TTC Code is matched against the value of the TTR colour use field, therefore giving the colour for the HTML timetable.
This table defines groups of Translation (TTR) records that are available to each group of users. The record also holds the defaults detailing how the record is viewed.

This table indicates the priority that individual records will be given when creating the timetable. Driving records will always be shown in place of driven records when showing the same data in a slot. The process will assume a link when the value of the driving key matches that of the driven key.
Timetable Translation is used to translate the fields of an entity that a user wishes to show in the timetable.

The Timetable Version (TTV) record defines the version of a timetable. It holds Timetable Constraint (TCO) records as well as information regarding the start and end times of the Timetable. This table is linked to the Timetable Model (TTM) record through the Timetable Version Link (TVL) record.

Defines different types of time usage employed in the system. The system does not currently use this table to the full and its expansion is reserved for the future. This is a system table which should not be changed by the user.

This table defines blocks of time when students may be unavailable for study. It is used by the top level Student Module Selections (SMS) screen when both selections and unavailability can be defined at the same time. The SMS screen is an alternative to the Student Module Selections and Student Unavailability screens accessed individually via the "Other" menu option in SPR. This method of input may be useful for inputting selections for students on similar but not necessarily identical patterns of study. It also has the advantage that it is not year/period specific and can be used over and over again, unlike the unavailability pattern (UAP,UAP>UAE) records which are time specific. Unavailability can be defined in terms of time and/or location.
Defines the individual time and location details which make up an unavailability record.

Defines patterns of unavailability which may be used on a regular basis or for large numbers of students. Patterns reduce the amount of keying in of data required for each student's unavailability record. This may be particularly useful where modules are offered during day and evening and there are students who can only attend in the evening. Unavailability patterns can be used to make students unavailable at a particular location for the full extent of the week. This would be done by entering the first day of the teaching week in the Start Day field and the last day in the End Day field, followed by the start and end times of the teaching day, followed by the location which is to be unavailable for the specified time.

Defines the conversion of marks and grades used in CAMS for module results and assessments into marks and grades used by external validating bodies such as BTEC. This table is used to make conversions from one marking system to another in intermediate, final transcripts and notification of performance reports.

Defines the different validating bodies used for the conferment of awards. The types of qualifications that can be obtained from the validating body are defined by the Qualification table which can only be accessed via the Validating Body table.

Variable Assessment Weighting. Alternative method in calculating the module result. Can choose or exclude assessment marks and choose a different weighting for the assessment chosen. The marks collected for calculation are held in descending order. Also qualifying set can be used to combine assessments to one whole assessment mark. Assessment Group included so that VAW calculation will only take effect for a given group. Note all weighting must add up to 100%, for those in a group must also add up to 100% Example ; Only take the two lowest mark with 50% each, from four possible assessment. Setup VAW records as follows. Sequence Weighting 001 0% 002 0% 003 50% 004 50%
Defines the external levels used for the validating body for the conversion of the internal levels used in the system. Conversion Credit Factor to change the current level of credits.

The Assessment to Schedule Element record is a list of the associated assessment data that has been used to create the parent Assessment to Schedule (WAS) record. This record is automatically maintained as part of the Generate Assessment and Reload processes within Exam Scheduling.
Warehouse Table Primary use for Learning Materials

The Assessment to Schedule Element Link (WAL) record is used to link an Assessment Person (WAP) with an Assessment to Schedule Element (WAE) record. This ensures a link between the Assessment Person (WAP) (a record to denote that a person is to be scheduled on a particular paper) and the module assessment(s) held in WAE that the person is undertaking that require that paper.
The Assessment Person (WAP) screen holds the person related data for WAS such as MST, STU and SPR code.

Windows Assessment Requirements Facilities Records  This table holds information about a student's exam requirements so that these requirements can be taken into account when scheduling exams.  The requirement (WARF) records are linked to the student's Windows Assessment Requirements (WAR) record.

The assessments to schedule records can be reviewed and minor modifications made if the requirements are not yet met. Individual invigilators can be added to Assessment to Schedule (WAS) records, which effectively assigns an invigilator to a module.
The Assessment Job Requirements (WJR) holds Institution-defined roles, which can be assigned to rooms to indicate requirements
The Week Pattern (WKP) table holds the unique week ranges defined in Topic Element (TEL) and Frequency Element (FQE) for the Academic Year. This information is then sent to the Module Scheduler.

The Assessment Room Near Match record is used by the exam scheduling process to find Rooms within a certain range of Student numbers.  When no records exist the process will look for an exact match between the seats available and the seats required.
The Room Splits (WRS) facility is used to determine the maximum number of rooms over which an individual module, within an assessment profile, can be split
The scheduling constraints table defines specific sets of controls, which can then be applied to scheduling profiles, assessment slots, and scheduling profile elements
Assessment Slot Definitions holds template records from which slots will be generated.

The Element record instructs the scheduler which assessments need to be included in the timetable. The element record also attaches further constraints upon the exams it picks up, such as a specific range of slots, or dates, that the exam has to be placed into. The element record is also one of the places that an alternative set of constraints or a room collection can be added.
The slots into which the examinations will be scheduled
The Assessment Slot Modules display the modules that are scheduled into each slot
The Assessment Scheduling Profile is the main default profile screen used for each exam schedule.
The Assessment Slot Students screen displays a list of students that occupy the slots for a particular Scheduling Profile.

Cross Credit Rule Elements are associated with a Cross Credit Rule (XCR) and hold information that specifies how the various course-length combinations should be dealt with by the Cross Crediting screen on e:Vision. This includes how many credits can be cross-credited and also which levels.

Associated with a Programme (XCR), the Cross Credit Rule table is the header record used to group all rules that apply to that programme together. These rules are used by the Cross-crediting screen on e:Vision to determine which, and how many credits can be cross-credited.
The York Assessment Compensation (YAC) entity is used to hold parameter values for use by the University of York in their bespoke Assessment Compensation processing.

Weekly Start Dates is used to automatically assign calendar dates to the weeks which make up a period.  When the periods are defined for a particular academic year CAMS can generate week records for the number of weeks specified for a period.  For this table to work correctly the AYR/AYW needs to have been defined and made available or unavailable.  You need only enter the Year Week the period week number is already there and the data is generated automatically.

The Period records define terms/semesters which make up a specific academic year, including the start and end dates and the number of staff hours on which staff related analyses are calculated. CAMS will then generate blank week records for the number of weeks specified for a period to which the calendar dates are then assigned in the Weekly Dates table.
The York Reassessment Opportunities (YRO) entity is used to hold parameter values for use by the University of York in their bespoke Reassessment Opportunities processing.
